correctness.rationale: The orthogonal sum of adjacency eigenspace kernels at the junction reduces both the adjacency matrix and the sink projection. On the complement, an eigenvector of the lossy generator with real eigenvalue would have junction coordinate zero by the imaginary part of its Rayleigh quotient, which is impossible there; all Jordan blocks on that complement decay. Deleting the junction gives two discrete paths. Dirichlet sine mode k has endpoint sum proportional to 1+(-1)^{k+1}, so the reflection-odd modes (even k) are already dark. Cosine is injective on the mode interval, so cross-petal equal energies are exactly k/m=l/n=q/d. An additional rank-one cancellation occurs precisely when both indices are odd. Normalizing its null vector of the junction coupling gives first-branch squared norm m/(m+n), hence site weight 2 sin²(pi q x/d)/(m+n). For odd d, pairing q and d−q halves the full sine-square sum; for even d the odd-index cosine sum vanishes except at x=0 or d/2 modulo d. At an even antipode with equal valuations the residue is d/2, giving a strictly positive d/(m+n). At all other nonjunction sites reflection alone gives 1/2; at the junction the projector vanishes. The independent exact rational projector check matched all 100 graph pairs (cycle lengths 3–12) and all 1400 site weights including junctions.

value.rationale: The discrete figure-eight is the minimal natural two-petal cycle geometry for one-junction coherent loss. Knowing mere eigenvalue degeneracies or antisymmetry does not decide exact trapped fraction at a site. The theorem gives the complete rank and local response and a sharp change from perfect capture to nonzero survival at an antipode under the two-adic resonance, independently of absorber rate. These are directly usable transport invariants on arbitrary lengths, not a tiny-instance projector check.
residual_risks: No finite-time performance, flux, disorder, or dephasing consequence is established.
